# Wave023 A — time uncertainty changes the grammar

Independent FIRST, 15 October 2026. Peer023 unread; no experiments/helpers/project changes. Canonical backlog/index and bounded historical rounds were inspected. Root's later native B/W metadata verification is accepted context (2 loads, 0 predict/fit), not source→score parity; original018 FAILED and real015 CLOSED remain unchanged.

**Dedup/disposition.** Zero new canonical HYPs. A023-R1 is an optional HYP-002 typed-generation refinement, related to rounds004/011/025/030/037/048/052 and my wave019 clock/capability canary. Those already require declared units, availability and timestamp precision. The bounded prior search did not find this particular interval-count production; that is a provisional local delta, not academic novelty or admission. HYP046 physical planning is not the claimed delta.

**mechanism.** One observable contract property selects operators: `time_kind=instant` versus explicitly supplied **bounded occurrence-time support** `[L,U]` in exact UTC ticks. Storage dtype or a midnight timestamp pattern cannot establish this meaning. Human review supplies the semantic declaration; schema/value checks can reject it. Arrow distinguishes semantic types, physical layouts and timestamp parameters; it does not infer occurrence uncertainty. [Arrow specification](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html).

For this first production, allow only raw action-counts on user/item/pair grains and human-listed windows. Require known row availability A and a declared post-occurrence reporting contract `L≤U≤A`; admit rows only when `A<a`, excluding all availability peers. For window `[b=a−w,a)`, generate two integer fields:

`C_lo = Σ 1[b≤L and U<a]`

`C_hi = Σ 1[U≥b and L<a]`

Both sums use the same available qualifying raw bag. They conservatively bracket counts over supported occurrence times; they are not confidence intervals or corrections for unseen events. Duplicates contribute separately. Point supports `L=U` recover exact counts. Empty observed bags give 0/0 with existing source-coverage information. Unknown availability rejects the binding; malformed/missing bounds in the available prefix reject that anchor, never silently zero/drop rows. Future unavailable malformed rows cannot alter an earlier output. Open/unbounded intervals are unsupported. Category-as-of, exact recency, DISTINCT and ratio productions remain unavailable in this branch; do not fabricate them. PostgreSQL documents explicit range endpoints and distinguishes unbounded bounds; it supplies representation semantics, not our feature algorithm. [Range documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/rangetypes.html).

**prediction.** Explicit interval support crossing a window boundary produces `C_lo<C_hi`; identical names with instant semantics produce exact counts. Example expectation, not a run: at `[10,20)`, support `[9,11]`, A=12 contributes 0/1, while point10 contributes1/1. An event available exactly20 contributes neither. This tests semantic adaptation, not ranking gain.

**nearest finite experiment — UNRUN.** One source-free canary: ≤12 invented rows, two otherwise identical manifests, two anchors/two windows, ≤16 AST definitions and ≤64 explicit supported-time assignments. Compare generated bounds and rejection decisions with independently written containment/intersection counts and hand expectations. Include duplicate bags, empty groups, lower-bound equality, global peers, missing/inverted bounds and unavailable future faults. Check every realized count lies between the bounds and instant supports collapse. The strongest simple control receives the same reviewed manifest and manually implements these two predicates; rename-only or midpoint adapters are weaker controls. Any mismatch rejects this production; collapse everywhere defers it as unnecessary representation.

**task1 benefit.** A passing canary would show one bounded grammar changes its available operators when temporal information changes, avoiding false exactness during transfer. No present REES46/Retailrocket interval binding was established; current B/W gains and015/018 are unaffected.

**Counterexample/cost.** Midnight events may be genuinely exact: widening them invents uncertainty. Even valid intervals can add no useful information. Future canary cap only:15 CPU seconds/30 wall seconds/128 MiB including manifest review, invalid attempts, enumeration, oracle and report; 0 fits/feedback/model/Y/native/source scans. Human review time must be logged separately. Production would read availability plus both bounds, validate every admitted row, perform two predicates/aggregates per leaf and retain O(K) group state, with two physical output columns. Authentication, source acquisition/validation, full scans, spill, materialization and review costs remain unmeasured and must be budgeted before any real use. This proposal grants nothing and adds no main prerequisite.

# Wave023 / author B — anonymous sessions change compatibility operators

Blind FIRST; no peer023 read. Bounded canonical backlog/index and round068 checked; assignment remains Root's message, with sole publisher `/root/backlog_coordinator`. No install/data/model/native/fit/Y/experiment/large hash/project write. Root's newer native-metadata verification is acknowledged; it grants no prediction or execution. Real015 CLOSED and original018 FAILED remain unchanged.

**Zero new mechanisms.** One Dressipi case refines HYP002/TLAB016 adapter generation, TLAB005, round013/040/068 and existing audience/UserCF notes. It does not introduce a recommender or another current-study search.

The official2022 schema supplies anonymous session/item/timestamp views without user_id; an item label per purchasing session; and item/feature-category/value tags. It discloses purchase-conditioned sampling, one randomly selected order item, target-related prefix truncation and a candidate set derived from test-month purchases. These facts prevent direct reuse as an unconditioned full24h purchase task. [Official challenge schema](https://www.recsyschallenge.com/2022/dataset.html). [Dressipi's provider page](https://dressipi.com/downloads/recsys-datasets/) confirms the public fashion-session dataset; no archive or license grant is inferred. Both read15 October2026.

## R023-E1 — unit-certified compatibility, existing-family refinement

| Field | Concrete content |
|---|---|
| mechanism | Bind aggregation/join keys to semantic capabilities: PersonKey, anonymous SessionKey, EventFact and multivalued TagRelation. Require each generated compatibility operator to declare its counting unit, temporal availability and conditioning population. Reject unsupported capabilities instead of renaming columns. |
| prediction | Person-audience/longitudinal user operators and exposure-normalized rates refuse this schema. Explicit session-prefix counts, distinct items and supplied-tag set overlap remain possible under a separately declared conditional-prefix task. A successful adapter preserves these differences rather than manufacturing B41. |
| nearest finite UNRUN experiment | Six-record role/fanout witness below, comparing capability-aware admission with a generic field-renaming adapter. Current exact005/016 schema validator should reject a drop-in Dressipi registry; positive tests concern a prospective adapter specification. |
| task1 benefit | Automatically generate only meaning-preserving feature families on another product dataset, with explainable refusals for tempting but unidentified user×item operators. |

Simple control: map session_id→user_id and feature_category_id→category_id. It mechanically admits familiar operators but changes their meaning. Two sessions could belong to one person or two; no provided field distinguishes those worlds. Distinct-session audience size is observable, distinct-person size is not. User repeat-purchase and cross-session profile carryover therefore fail; session-neighbor compatibility may be defined explicitly, without pretending it is person similarity.

Documented views are positive observations, not a count of shown opportunities. Refuse CTR, propensity/exposure normalization and causal interest claims. Supplied content tags can be multivalued; they are not a single product category or automatically historical as-of metadata. Use them only under a declared supplied-snapshot assumption. A challenge candidate artifact may define its own conditional task, but cannot certify a past-available catalog or replace current REES46 C.

Literal witness: three views `(s1,a,τ1),(s2,a,τ2),(s3,b,τ3)`, two tags `(a,red),(a,blue)`, one query-prefix descriptor for s3. Alternative hidden person maps give one versus two people for a, with identical observable records; distinct sessions is2 in both. Joining tags before event counting turns two a-view rows into four. Aggregate EventFact multiplicity before tag joining; do not deduplicate tuples to invent event IDs. Equal-time peers remain unordered; no unseen suffix enters the prefix.

Proposed finite work: six operator requests over six supplied records,≤8 expanded nodes/request,≤288 primitive evaluations plus≤36 join-pair checks, zero source scans/models/fits/Y. Include schema/semantic mapping, snapshot/clock declaration, complete support/NULL closure, independent expected values, diagnostics and code/spec authentication;≤5CPU minutes/256MiB is an ungranted future ceiling. Missing timezone, receipt time or purchase-time support remains unknown, not inferred from row order.

False person/exposure admission or fanout-corrupted counts rejects the adapter. Safe refusal with legal session/tag operations confirms only specification conformance; predictive transfer remains untested. No additional task, framework,015/018 prerequisite or current-study authority follows.
